overview.description: A multi-agent consensus trading system (the 'Parliament') where five specialized AI agents independently analyze prediction market opportunities through isolated information contexts, then vote on whether to execute each trade. The architecture leverages Claude Code's native infrastructure — MCP servers for live data, CLAUDE.md for immutable trading rules, the skill system for typed capabilities, and subagent orchestration for parallel execution. Each agent specializes in a distinct analytical domain (geopolitics, macroeconomics, science, sports, crypto), receives domain-specific data feeds, and produces a structured vote with confidence score and reasoning. A consensus threshold of 3/5 agents must agree before execution. Critically, dissenting minority votes are treated as high-value signals rather than noise — when a single agent dissents against four, a 5-sample pilot showed it was correct 4 out of 5 times (80%), though this sample size is insufficient for statistical reliability and must be validated over 30+ solo-dissent events. The system targets a 20%+ ROI improvement over single-agent approaches by eliminating overconfident single-model failures and filtering out low-conviction trades at the gate.
objectives: Outperform single-agent trading by 20%+ ROI through ensemble consensus filtering
Eliminate single-model overconfidence by requiring adversarial validation across 5 specialized agents
Reduce average loss size by 50% through consensus gating — refuse entry when agents cannot agree
Increase win rate from ~60% (single-agent baseline) to 74%+ through multi-perspective analysis
Surface high-value dissent signals — minority votes that contradict majority consensus as early warning indicators
Enable fully autonomous 24/7 execution with no human intervention required for standard trades
Implement Kelly Criterion position sizing derived from per-agent confidence scores and historical wallet pattern analysis
Support cross-market arbitrage detection across Polymarket, Kalshi, and correlated outcome pairs
Provide progressive signal loading so agents can be added/removed without rebuilding the system
Maintain full audit trail of all votes, dissent reports, and execution decisions for iterative improvement
constraints: Each agent MUST operate in an isolated information context — shared information collapses diversity and defeats the purpose
Minimum consensus threshold of 3/5 agents required for any trade execution
Maximum risk per position governed by CLAUDE.md rules — no agent can override the risk ceiling
All agents must return structured output: direction (YES/NO/ABSTAIN), confidence (0-100), reasoning (text), and sources (array)
Dissent reports are mandatory when the parliament splits — minority agents must produce counterarguments with specific sources
Kelly Criterion sizing with a fractional cap (half-Kelly or quarter-Kelly) to prevent catastrophic drawdown
System must handle API rate limits, network failures, and agent timeouts gracefully with fallback to NO_TRADE

Latency budget: full parliament vote cycle targets p50=60s, p95=120s. The 30-second per-agent timeout will produce frequent ABSTAINs on complex markets; to mitigate, Market Scanner must pre-fetch and cache all domain-specific data feeds at scan time so agents receive pre-loaded data packages rather than fetching live during their analysis window. Agents should spend their 30 seconds on analysis, not data retrieval.
No agent may access another agent's raw analysis — only the orchestrator sees all votes
Human override capability must exist for emergency halt, but standard operation is fully autonomous
assumptions: Claude Code with MCP server support is available as the execution environment
Polymarket API provides real-time order book, contract data, and execution endpoints
Each agent can be instantiated as a separate Claude subagent with its own system prompt and tool access
External data feeds (diplomatic briefings, Fed minutes, whale alerts, Twitter sentiment, sports feeds) are accessible via dedicated MCP servers or API integrations
Historical wallet analysis of top performers has been completed to derive Kelly sizing parameters
The system operates with sufficient capital to absorb losing streaks within Kelly-sized positions
Market liquidity is sufficient for the position sizes the system will attempt
Agent specialization domains (geopolitics, macro, science, sports, crypto) cover the majority of prediction market categories on target platforms

components.name: Orchestrator (Parliament Speaker)
components.description: The central coordination layer that manages the full trade evaluation lifecycle. Receives candidate markets from the Market Scanner, distributes them to all 5 specialist agents in parallel, collects structured votes, applies consensus logic, triggers dissent report generation when splits occur, computes aggregate confidence, determines Kelly-sized position, and dispatches execution orders. Implements the harness architecture pattern from claw-code: runtime context scoping with typed I/O contracts and scoped agent permissions. The orchestrator never makes trading decisions itself — it is purely a coordination and aggregation layer.
responsibilities: Receive candidate markets from Market Scanner
Fan out market data to all 5 specialist agents in parallel via subagent dispatch
Collect structured vote responses with timeout handling (30s per agent, fallback to ABSTAIN)
Apply consensus threshold logic: 3/5 minimum agreement for execution
Trigger mandatory dissent report generation on split votes (3:2 or 4:1)
Compute weighted aggregate confidence from individual agent scores
Calculate Kelly-sized position based on aggregate probability estimate and current bankroll
Dispatch execution orders to the Execution Engine
Log all votes, reasoning, dissent reports, and decisions to the Audit Trail
Implement circuit breakers: halt trading if daily loss limit reached or if win rate drops below threshold over rolling window
interfaces: Input: CandidateMarket from Market Scanner
Output: ParliamentDecision {direction, aggregate_confidence, position_size, votes[], dissent_reports[]}
Output: ExecutionOrder to Execution Engine
Output: AuditEntry to Audit Trail

components.name: Market Scanner
components.description: Continuously monitors target platforms (Polymarket, Kalshi) for tradeable opportunities. Scans all active markets at configurable intervals (default: every 15 minutes), filters by liquidity minimums, volume thresholds, and time-to-resolution. Identifies cross-market arbitrage opportunities where paired contracts (YES + NO) deviate from $1.00, or where the same event is priced differently across platforms. Outputs a ranked list of CandidateMarket objects to the Orchestrator. Inspired by the PHANTOM system's approach of tracking thousands of markets simultaneously and the wallet analysis agent's pattern of scanning 147 contracts per session.
responsibilities: Poll Polymarket and Kalshi APIs for active markets at configurable intervals
Filter markets by minimum liquidity ($5K+ volume), minimum time-to-resolution (>2 hours), and maximum spread
Detect cross-market arbitrage: paired contract deviations from $1.00 (risk-free arb opportunities)
Detect cross-platform arbitrage: same event priced differently on Polymarket vs Kalshi
Rank candidates by estimated edge magnitude and liquidity
Apply CLAUDE.md liquidity filters and excluded-market rules
Pass CandidateMarket objects to Orchestrator with full market metadata as JSON
interfaces: Input: Raw market data from Polymarket MCP Server and Kalshi MCP Server
Output: CandidateMarket {market_id, platform, name, current_odds, deadline, volume, category, paired_contract_data, cross_platform_price}

components.name: Geopolitics Agent
components.description: Analyzes markets through a geopolitical lens. Receives diplomatic briefings, sanctions lists, treaty status updates, UN voting records, and geopolitical risk indices. Specializes in elections, international conflicts, sanctions outcomes, diplomatic negotiations, and government policy decisions. Operates in a completely isolated context — does NOT see on-chain data, does NOT read social media sentiment, does NOT access sports or science feeds. This isolation is fundamental to preserving analytical diversity.
responsibilities: Receive CandidateMarket JSON from Orchestrator with geopolitics-specific data feeds attached
Analyze market through geopolitical framework: power dynamics, historical precedent, institutional incentives
Assess probability of outcome based on diplomatic signals, intelligence assessments, and policy trajectories
Return structured vote: {direction: YES|NO|ABSTAIN, confidence: 0-100, reasoning: string, sources: string[], domain_signals: object}
When in minority on a split vote, produce dissent report with specific counterarguments and source citations
data_feeds: Diplomatic briefings and press releases (via news MCP server)
Sanctions lists and trade policy updates
UN voting records and Security Council proceedings
Geopolitical risk indices (e.g., GPR index)
Government official statements and policy announcements
components.system_prompt_scope: You are a geopolitical analyst specializing in prediction market assessment. You evaluate markets ONLY through the lens of international relations, political power dynamics, institutional incentives, and diplomatic signals. You do NOT have access to financial market data, on-chain metrics, social media sentiment, sports statistics, or scientific research. Your analysis must cite specific geopolitical sources and events. Return your assessment as structured JSON.

components.name: Macroeconomics Agent
components.description: Analyzes markets through a macroeconomic lens. Receives Fed minutes, CPI/PPI data, employment reports, GDP figures, yield curve data, and central bank communications. Specializes in economic policy outcomes, inflation bets, interest rate decisions, recession probabilities, and fiscal policy impacts. Isolated from social media, on-chain data, and domain-specific feeds outside economics.
responsibilities: Receive CandidateMarket JSON from Orchestrator with macroeconomics-specific data feeds attached
Analyze market through macroeconomic framework: monetary policy, fiscal dynamics, leading indicators
Assess probability using economic models, historical base rates, and indicator convergence
Return structured vote: {direction: YES|NO|ABSTAIN, confidence: 0-100, reasoning: string, sources: string[], domain_signals: object}
When in minority on a split vote, produce dissent report with specific economic counterarguments
data_feeds: Federal Reserve minutes, speeches, and dot plots
CPI, PPI, PCE inflation data
Employment reports (NFP, unemployment rate, JOLTS)
GDP and GDI estimates
Treasury yield curve and credit spreads
Central bank communications from ECB, BOJ, BOE
components.system_prompt_scope: You are a macroeconomic analyst specializing in prediction market assessment. You evaluate markets ONLY through the lens of monetary policy, fiscal policy, economic indicators, and central bank dynamics. You do NOT have access to social media, on-chain data, sports statistics, or geopolitical intelligence beyond what affects economic policy. Return your assessment as structured JSON.

components.name: Science & Technology Agent
components.description: Analyzes markets through a scientific and technological lens. Receives research publications, clinical trial data, patent filings, regulatory submissions (FDA, EMA), and technology adoption curves. Specializes in scientific breakthroughs, drug approvals, technology milestones, climate events, and space/defense technology outcomes. The most contrarian agent in historical testing — voted against the majority on 40% of markets, and when it was the sole dissenter against 4 agents, it was correct 80% of the time (4 out of 5 events). NOTE: The 80% figure is from a 5-sample pilot and cannot be treated as statistically reliable. This metric must be re-evaluated after 30+ solo-dissent events are observed before being used to drive automated decisions. This makes it a potentially high-value agent for preventing catastrophic losses, pending validation at scale.
responsibilities: Receive CandidateMarket JSON from Orchestrator with science-specific data feeds attached
Analyze market through scientific rigor: evidence quality, replication likelihood, regulatory precedent, technical feasibility
Assess probability using base rates for scientific claims, clinical trial success rates by phase, and technology readiness levels
Return structured vote: {direction: YES|NO|ABSTAIN, confidence: 0-100, reasoning: string, sources: string[], domain_signals: object}
When in minority, produce especially detailed dissent reports — historical data shows this agent's dissent is the highest-value signal in the entire system
data_feeds: PubMed / arXiv preprints and publications
FDA and EMA regulatory filings and advisory committee votes
Clinical trial registries (ClinicalTrials.gov) with phase and endpoint data
Patent filings and technology readiness assessments
Satellite and meteorological data for climate/weather markets
components.system_prompt_scope: You are a scientific analyst specializing in prediction market assessment. You evaluate markets ONLY through the lens of empirical evidence, scientific methodology, regulatory precedent, and technological feasibility. You are naturally skeptical of claims that lack strong evidence. You apply base rate reasoning aggressively. You do NOT have access to financial data, social media, geopolitical intelligence, or sports statistics. When you disagree with a market's implied probability, state your case with maximum specificity. Return your assessment as structured JSON.

components.name: Sports Agent
components.description: Analyzes markets through a sports analytics lens. Receives team/player statistics, injury reports, historical matchup data, venue effects, and sports-specific quantitative models. Specializes in game outcomes, player performance, tournament brackets, and over/under markets. Particularly valuable for detecting arbitrage in paired O/U contracts where YES + NO should sum to $1.00 but frequently deviate due to differential trader reaction speeds (the PHANTOM strategy).
responsibilities: Receive CandidateMarket JSON from Orchestrator with sports-specific data feeds attached
Analyze market through sports analytics framework: Elo ratings, injury-adjusted projections, venue effects, schedule fatigue
Detect paired contract mispricing: if YES costs $0.62 and NO costs $0.41, total is $1.03 = 3% risk-free arb
Assess probability using statistical models, not narrative or media hype
Return structured vote: {direction: YES|NO|ABSTAIN, confidence: 0-100, reasoning: string, sources: string[], domain_signals: object, arb_detected: boolean, arb_spread: number}
When in minority on a split vote, produce dissent report grounded in statistical evidence
data_feeds: Team and player statistics databases (ESPN, Sports Reference)
Real-time injury reports and lineup confirmations
Historical head-to-head matchup data
Venue and travel schedule data
Betting line movements from traditional sportsbooks for calibration
components.system_prompt_scope: You are a sports analytics specialist evaluating prediction market contracts. You assess outcomes ONLY through quantitative sports analysis: Elo ratings, win probability models, injury-adjusted projections, and schedule effects. You actively look for paired contract arbitrage (YES + NO > $1.00 or < $1.00). You do NOT access geopolitical, economic, or crypto data. Return your assessment as structured JSON.

components.name: Crypto & On-Chain Agent
components.description: Analyzes markets through a crypto-native lens. Receives whale alerts, on-chain flow data, DeFi protocol metrics, Twitter/X crypto sentiment scores, and smart money wallet tracking. Specializes in crypto price outcomes, DeFi governance votes, protocol milestones, regulatory decisions affecting crypto, and on-chain activity patterns. Derived from the wallet analysis methodology: analyzing 10K+ top wallets, cross-referencing win rates and sizing patterns to identify edges that are skill rather than luck.
responsibilities: Receive CandidateMarket JSON from Orchestrator with crypto-specific data feeds attached
Analyze market through on-chain lens: whale positioning, smart money flows, protocol fundamentals, sentiment divergence
Track top wallet behavior patterns — identify when smart money is positioning on specific outcomes
Assess probability using on-chain evidence, not price charts or narratives
Return structured vote: {direction: YES|NO|ABSTAIN, confidence: 0-100, reasoning: string, sources: string[], domain_signals: object, whale_alignment: number}
When in minority on a split vote, produce dissent report citing specific on-chain evidence
data_feeds: Whale alert feeds (large transaction monitoring)
On-chain flow analysis (exchange inflows/outflows)
Twitter/X crypto sentiment scores (aggregated, not raw)
Smart money wallet tracking (top 100 wallets by ROI on Polymarket)
DeFi protocol TVL, governance proposals, and treasury data
Gas fee trends and network congestion metrics
components.system_prompt_scope: You are a crypto and on-chain analyst specializing in prediction market assessment. You evaluate markets ONLY through on-chain data, whale behavior, smart money wallet patterns, DeFi fundamentals, and crypto-native sentiment. You track what the most profitable wallets are doing, not what influencers are saying. You do NOT access geopolitical briefings, macroeconomic data, sports statistics, or scientific publications. Return your assessment as structured JSON.

components.name: Execution Engine
components.description: Handles all trade execution after the Parliament approves a position. Manages order placement, slippage control, partial fill handling, and position tracking. Implements the three execution strategies identified in the PHANTOM analysis: direct market orders for high-conviction consensus trades, limit orders for lower-urgency positions, and millisecond-speed arbitrage execution for paired contract mispricing. Connects to platform APIs via MCP servers. Sends Telegram alerts on fills, drawdown warnings, and daily P&L summaries.
responsibilities: Receive ExecutionOrder from Orchestrator with approved position size and direction
Place orders via Polymarket MCP Server and/or Kalshi MCP Server
Implement slippage protection: reject execution if price has moved more than 2% from analysis time
Handle partial fills gracefully — re-queue remainder or cancel based on time sensitivity
Track all open positions with real-time P&L
Execute paired contract arbitrage at maximum speed when Sports Agent detects mispricing
Send Telegram alerts on: order fills, position closures, drawdown threshold crossings, daily P&L summary
Implement emergency halt: cease all trading and close positions if daily loss exceeds CLAUDE.md limit

GRACEFUL SHUTDOWN: On system halt (manual, circuit breaker, or crash recovery): (1) Cancel all pending/open orders immediately, (2) Log all open position states to persistent storage (SQLite) with current market prices, (3) Do NOT auto-close positions on shutdown — positions on prediction markets cannot be 'closed' without selling at current market price which may realize unnecessary losses, (4) On restart, validate persisted state against live platform positions via MCP server queries before resuming trading, (5) Send Telegram alert with shutdown reason and open position summary, (6) Require explicit human confirmation before resuming autonomous trading after an unclean shutdown
interfaces: Input: ExecutionOrder {market_id, platform, direction, size_usd, limit_price, order_type, urgency}
Output: ExecutionResult {order_id, fill_price, fill_size, status, timestamp}
Output: TelegramAlert via webhook
Output: PositionUpdate to Portfolio Tracker

components.name: Portfolio Tracker & Risk Manager
components.description: Maintains real-time portfolio state, enforces risk limits, and tracks performance metrics against benchmarks. Computes rolling win rate, average win/loss ratio, Sharpe ratio equivalent, and maximum drawdown. Inspired by the $50K Claude Portfolio concept of live, transparent performance tracking. Enforces all CLAUDE.md risk rules as hard constraints that no agent or orchestrator can override.
responsibilities: Maintain real-time portfolio state: all open positions, cash balance, total equity
Enforce maximum position size (from CLAUDE.md rules) — reject orders that exceed per-trade or total exposure limits
Track rolling performance metrics: win rate, avg win/loss, total ROI, max drawdown, Sharpe-equivalent
Compare performance against single-agent baseline to measure parliament alpha
Implement drawdown circuit breaker: pause trading if drawdown exceeds configurable threshold (e.g., 15% of bankroll)
Generate daily performance report with per-agent accuracy breakdown
Track which agent's dissent was correct retroactively — update agent credibility scores over time

EXIT MANAGER: Monitor open positions for early exit conditions — cut losses when position moves against by configurable threshold (default: 15% of position value), take profit when position reaches configurable target (default: 2x edge captured), and trigger re-evaluation when material new information arrives (breaking news, data feed alert, or agent-initiated signal)

EXIT MANAGER: Maintain per-position exit rules at entry time: stop-loss price, take-profit price, and re-evaluation triggers. Dispatch a reduced parliament session (3 agents, 15-second timeout) for re-evaluation votes on whether to hold, exit, or adjust size
EXIT MANAGER: Execute early exits via Execution Engine with same slippage protections as entry orders. Log exit rationale to Audit Trail with entry-vs-exit P&L attribution
interfaces: Input: PositionUpdate from Execution Engine
Input: MarketResolution events from platform APIs
Input: ExitTrigger {position_id, trigger_type: 'stop_loss'|'take_profit'|'re_evaluation'|'manual', trigger_data}
Output: PortfolioState {equity, cash, positions[], metrics{}}
Output: RiskVeto — can block ExecutionOrders that violate risk limits
Output: ExitOrder {position_id, direction, size, reason, exit_type} to Execution Engine
Output: PerformanceReport (daily/weekly)

components.name: Dissent Analyzer
components.description: A meta-analytical component that specifically processes and weights dissent signals. When the parliament splits, this component analyzes the minority dissent reports, cross-references them with historical outcomes, and assigns a 'dissent quality score' that can modify the Orchestrator's final decision. Based on the empirical finding that the Science Agent's solo dissent against 4 agreeing agents was correct 4 out of 5 times — saving $890 in avoided losses from a single agent's contrarian signal. The Dissent Analyzer turns this pattern from anecdote into systematic edge.
responsibilities: Receive all dissent reports from minority-voting agents
Score dissent quality based on: specificity of sources cited, historical accuracy of the dissenting agent on similar markets, strength of counterargument
Maintain per-agent dissent accuracy tracking: when agent X dissents, how often is X ultimately correct?

Flag 'high-quality dissent' scenarios: e.g., Science Agent sole dissenter with >80 confidence = historically 80% accurate (5-sample pilot — do not trust accuracy score for automated escalation decisions until minimum 30 solo-dissent events per agent have been recorded; until then, always escalate to HUMAN_REVIEW rather than auto-ABORT or auto-PROCEED)
Can escalate dissent to human review or reduce position size when dissent quality score exceeds threshold
Feed dissent accuracy data back to Orchestrator for dynamic confidence weighting
interfaces: Input: DissentReport {agent_name, vote, confidence, reasoning, sources, market_context}
Output: DissentScore {quality: 0-100, historical_accuracy: float, recommendation: PROCEED|REDUCE_SIZE|HUMAN_REVIEW|ABORT}
Output: AgentCredibilityUpdate to Orchestrator

components.name: Audit Trail & Learning System
components.description: Persistent storage and analysis of all parliament decisions, agent votes, market outcomes, and performance attribution. Enables retroactive analysis of which agents were right, which dissent signals had value, and how consensus quality correlates with outcome. This is the learning loop that allows the system to improve over time by adjusting agent credibility weights and consensus thresholds based on empirical results.
responsibilities: Log every parliament session: market analyzed, all 5 votes with reasoning, consensus outcome, execution decision, final P&L
Track market resolutions and attribute outcomes to individual agent accuracy
Compute rolling accuracy by agent, by market category, and by consensus split pattern
Identify systematic biases: is any agent consistently overconfident? Consistently wrong on a market type?
Generate weekly learning reports recommending adjustments to agent weights or data feeds
Store all data in SQLite with structured schemas for downstream analysis and model fine-tuning
interfaces: Input: ParliamentSession {market, votes[], decision, execution, outcome}
Output: SQLite audit records (append-only, structured schemas)
Output: WeeklyLearningReport with recommendations
Output: AgentAccuracyMetrics for dynamic weight adjustment

architecture.data_flow: 1. MARKET DISCOVERY: Market Scanner polls Polymarket/Kalshi APIs via MCP servers every 15 minutes. Filters by CLAUDE.md liquidity and volume rules. Produces ranked CandidateMarket objects. 2. PROGRESSIVE SIGNAL LOADING: For each CandidateMarket, the Orchestrator prepares 5 isolated data packages — each containing the base market JSON (name, odds, deadline, volume) plus domain-specific feeds unique to that agent. Geopolitics gets diplomatic briefings; Macro gets Fed minutes and CPI; Science gets clinical trials and research; Sports gets stats and injury reports; Crypto gets whale alerts and on-chain flows. No agent sees another agent's data. 3. PARALLEL AGENT DISPATCH: Orchestrator dispatches all 5 specialist agents simultaneously as Claude Code subagents. Each runs in its own context with its own system prompt. 30-second timeout per agent; timeout = ABSTAIN vote. 4. VOTE COLLECTION: Each agent returns structured JSON: {direction, confidence, reasoning, sources, domain_signals}. Orchestrator collects all 5 votes. 5. CONSENSUS EVALUATION: Orchestrator applies threshold: 3/5 minimum agreement on direction. If threshold not met, NO_TRADE and log the disagreement. 6. DISSENT PROCESSING: On split votes (3:2 or 4:1), minority agents produce dissent reports. Dissent Analyzer scores quality and checks historical accuracy of the dissenting agent(s). High-quality dissent can reduce position size or escalate to human review. 7. POSITION SIZING: If consensus reached, Orchestrator computes Kelly-sized position using aggregate probability estimate (confidence-weighted average of agreeing agents) against market odds, capped at half-Kelly. Portfolio Tracker validates against risk limits. 8. EXECUTION: Execution Engine places order via platform MCP server. Slippage check, fill confirmation, Telegram alert. 9. RESOLUTION TRACKING: When market resolves, Audit Trail records outcome, attributes accuracy to each agent, updates credibility scores. 10. LEARNING LOOP: Weekly, the system reviews agent accuracy by domain and market category, adjusts credibility weights, and flags agents that need data feed improvements.

integration_points.name: Polymarket MCP Server
integration_points.description: MCP server wrapping Polymarket's CLOB API. Provides real-time order book, contract data, market listings, and order execution endpoints. Registered in .mcp.json. Tools: get_markets, get_order_book, get_contract, place_order, cancel_order, get_positions, get_trade_history.
tools: polymarket_place_order(market_id, side, size, price, type) -> OrderResult

integration_points.name: Kalshi MCP Server
integration_points.description: MCP server wrapping Kalshi's API for cross-platform arbitrage detection and execution. Provides event listings, market data, and order management.

integration_points.name: News & Intelligence MCP Server
integration_points.description: Aggregates news feeds, diplomatic briefings, and real-time event data. Provides filtered, domain-specific news queries so each agent only receives data relevant to its specialization. Prevents information cross-contamination between agents.
tools: news_query(domain: 'geopolitics'|'economics'|'science'|'sports'|'crypto', query: string, hours_back?: number) -> Article[]
news_get_sentiment(topic: string) -> SentimentScore{positive, negative, neutral, magnitude}

integration_points.name: On-Chain Analytics MCP Server
integration_points.description: Provides on-chain data feeds for the Crypto Agent. Whale alerts, wallet tracking, DeFi metrics, and exchange flow analysis.
tools: onchain_polymarket_smart_money(top_n?: number) -> SmartWallet[]{address, roi, win_rate, recent_positions[]}

integration_points.name: Telegram Notification Webhook
integration_points.description: Sends real-time alerts to a Telegram channel/chat. Used for order fill notifications, drawdown warnings, daily P&L summaries, and high-quality dissent alerts that may require human review.
events: dissent_escalation: high-quality dissent flagged for human review
daily_summary: end-of-day P&L, win rate, positions

integration_points.name: X (Twitter) API MCP Server
integration_points.description: Existing custom MCP server wrapping X API v2 with OAuth PKCE, registered in .mcp.json. Used by the Crypto Agent for sentiment analysis and by the Sports Agent for real-time injury/lineup news. Provides search, user lookup, and thread retrieval. NOTE: Agents sharing this MCP server must use non-overlapping query namespaces to preserve information isolation. The Crypto Agent should search only crypto-specific terms (e.g., $BTC, DeFi, whale alert) and the Sports Agent only sports-specific terms (e.g., injury report, lineup, game day). The Orchestrator's data package preparation must enforce these query scopes — agents must not be able to craft arbitrary X API queries that breach their domain boundary.

phases.name: Foundation — MCP Servers & CLAUDE.md Rules
phases.description: Set up the infrastructure layer: configure MCP servers for Polymarket API, deploy CLAUDE.md trading rules, and establish the project structure.
deliverables: Kalshi MCP Server (read-only baseline): event listings and market data endpoints registered in .mcp.json. Kalshi has a simpler REST API and should be integrated first to validate the MCP server pattern before tackling Polymarket.

Polymarket MCP Server: live market data, order book, execution endpoints registered in .mcp.json. NOTE: Polymarket execution requires a dedicated wallet, EIP-712 typed data signing for order placement, and CLOB API key registration. Budget additional setup time for wallet/signing infrastructure — this is significantly more complex than a standard REST API wrapper.
CLAUDE.md trading rules file with immutable constraints (see claude_md_rules below)
Project directory structure: /agents, /skills, /orchestrator, /execution, /data, /config
Basic Market Scanner skill: polls markets, filters by CLAUDE.md rules, outputs CandidateMarket JSON
Integration tests validating MCP server connectivity and data quality

phases.name: Agent Parliament — Specialist Agents & Voting
phases.description: Build the 5 specialist agents with isolated system prompts, domain-specific data feed routing, and structured vote output. Implement the Orchestrator's parallel dispatch and vote collection.
deliverables: 5 specialist agent definitions with system prompts, tool permissions, and data feed configurations
Orchestrator service: parallel subagent dispatch, timeout handling, vote collection
Structured vote schema with validation: direction, confidence, reasoning, sources, domain_signals
Consensus threshold logic: 3/5 minimum, weighted confidence aggregation
Dry-run mode: full parliament evaluation without execution, outputting vote logs for manual review

phases.name: Dissent & Sizing — Contrarian Signal Processing
phases.description: Build the dissent reporting system, Dissent Analyzer, Kelly Criterion sizing, and Portfolio Tracker. This is where the system's edge over single-agent approaches materializes.
deliverables: Mandatory dissent report generation for split-vote scenarios
Dissent Analyzer with quality scoring and historical accuracy tracking
Kelly Criterion position sizer with fractional cap (half-Kelly default)
Portfolio Tracker with real-time P&L, risk limits enforcement, and drawdown circuit breaker
Dissent escalation to Telegram for human review on high-quality minority signals

phases.name: Execution & Monitoring — Live Trading Pipeline
phases.description: Connect the full pipeline from Market Scanner through Parliament through Execution Engine. Deploy Telegram alerts, audit logging, and performance dashboards.
deliverables: Execution Engine with slippage protection, partial fill handling, and order management
Telegram notification integration for all event types
Audit Trail with SQLite-backed structured logging of all parliament sessions
Cross-market arbitrage fast path for paired contract mispricing
Paper trading validation: run full system on live markets with no real capital for 7 days minimum

phases.name: Learning & Optimization — Adaptive Weights
phases.description: Deploy the learning loop that adjusts agent credibility weights based on empirical outcomes. Expand to additional platforms and market categories. Target: measurable 20%+ ROI improvement over single-agent baseline.
deliverables: Weekly learning reports with per-agent accuracy breakdown by market category
Dynamic credibility weighting: agents that are consistently right on specific market types get higher vote weight
Kalshi MCP Server integration for cross-platform arbitrage
Additional data feed MCP servers as needed based on agent performance gaps

A/B testing framework: run parliament vs single-agent on identical markets for direct comparison. PREREQUISITE: Define and freeze a baseline_configuration for the single-agent comparison — must specify exact model version, system prompt text, data feeds, position sizing method, and risk limits. The baseline must be frozen before A/B testing begins and never modified during the comparison period, or results are invalid.
Performance benchmark dashboard comparing parliament ROI vs single-agent baseline

tech_stack: Claude Code — primary development and execution environment, provides subagent orchestration, skill system, and MCP integration
Python 3.12+ — agent harness implementation, data processing, and execution engine
MCP (Model Context Protocol) — standardized tool interface for all external data and execution APIs
Polymarket CLOB API — prediction market data and order execution
Kalshi API — secondary prediction market for cross-platform arbitrage
Claude API (Anthropic SDK) — for programmatic subagent instantiation when running outside Claude Code
JSON — structured data interchange format for all agent I/O, vote schemas, and audit logs
Telegram Bot API — real-time notifications and alerts

SQLite — audit trail, performance data persistence, and position state. Single source of truth for all structured data; JSON file storage is not acceptable for production audit trails due to lack of transactional integrity and concurrent access safety.
Git — version control for agent prompts, CLAUDE.md rules, and configuration

skill_definitions.description: Calculates implied probability, edge, and expected value for a given prediction market contract. Used by Market Scanner and individual agents.
skill_definitions.outputs: MarketAnalysis {implied_prob, edge_vs_fair, expected_value, liquidity_grade, time_to_resolution, recommendation}
skill_definitions.invocation: Claude Code skill invoked via /market-analyzer or programmatically by Orchestrator

skill_definitions.description: Computes optimal position size using Kelly Criterion given estimated probability, market odds, and current bankroll. Applies fractional Kelly cap.
skill_definitions.formula: f* = (p * b - q) / b, where p = estimated probability, q = 1-p, b = net odds. For binary YES contracts on prediction markets, b = (1 - p_market) / p_market, where p_market is the market price of the YES contract. Example: if our estimated probability is p=0.70 and the market price is p_market=0.55 (YES contract costs $0.55), then b = (1 - 0.55) / 0.55 = 0.818, and f* = (0.70 * 0.818 - 0.30) / 0.818 = (0.573 - 0.30) / 0.818 = 0.334, meaning Kelly-optimal is 33.4% of bankroll (before fractional cap). At half-Kelly, position size = 16.7% of bankroll, further capped by max_position_pct.

skill_definitions.description: Generates a structured dissent report when an agent is in the minority on a split vote. Forces the agent to produce specific counterarguments with source citations.
skill_definitions.inputs: DissentInput {agent_name, agent_vote, majority_direction, market_data, agent_reasoning, agent_sources}
skill_definitions.outputs: DissentReport {counterarguments: string[], risk_factors: string[], sources: string[], confidence_in_dissent: 0-100, recommended_action: 'proceed'|'reduce_size'|'abort'}

skill_definitions.description: Orchestrates a complete parliament voting session for a single market. Dispatches all 5 agents in parallel, collects votes, applies consensus logic, processes dissent, computes position size, and returns a final decision.
skill_definitions.inputs: SessionInput {candidate_market: CandidateMarket, bankroll: number, risk_limits: RiskLimits}
skill_definitions.outputs: SessionOutput {decision: 'EXECUTE'|'NO_TRADE'|'HUMAN_REVIEW', votes: Vote[], dissent_reports: DissentReport[], position_size_usd: number, aggregate_confidence: number, execution_order?: ExecutionOrder}

skill_definitions.description: Detects arbitrage opportunities in paired contracts (YES + NO != $1.00) and cross-platform price discrepancies for the same event.

claude_md_rules.description: Immutable trading rules enforced via CLAUDE.md. These are loaded into every agent's context at runtime and cannot be overridden by any agent or the orchestrator. They represent hard risk management constraints.

rules.name: Maximum Position Size
rules.rule: Never risk more than 5% of total bankroll on a single position. This applies regardless of confidence score or consensus strength.
rules.enforcement: Portfolio Tracker validates before execution; Execution Engine rejects oversized orders

rules.name: Minimum Edge Threshold
rules.rule: Do not enter any position where estimated edge is less than 7% (difference between estimated probability and implied market probability). Below this threshold, transaction costs and model uncertainty consume the edge.
rules.enforcement: Orchestrator checks edge calculation before dispatching ExecutionOrder

rules.name: Liquidity Floor
rules.rule: Do not trade markets with less than $5,000 in 24-hour volume or where the order book spread exceeds 8%. Illiquid markets create slippage risk that destroys edge.
rules.enforcement: Market Scanner filters out illiquid markets before they reach the Parliament

rules.name: Daily Loss Limit
rules.rule: If cumulative daily losses exceed 10% of starting-day bankroll, halt all trading for the remainder of the day. No exceptions. Resume at midnight UTC.
rules.enforcement: Portfolio Tracker monitors intraday P&L; Execution Engine implements hard halt

rules.name: Consensus Requirement
rules.rule: Minimum 3 out of 5 agents must agree on direction before any trade is executed. This threshold CANNOT be lowered. 2:3 splits or worse result in NO_TRADE. EXCEPTION: Verified paired-contract arbitrage (YES + NO < $0.98 after fees on same market, or equivalent cross-platform price discrepancy) may bypass consensus requirement because the edge is mathematically defined, not probabilistic. Arbitrage bypass requires: (1) spread exceeds 2% after all fees, (2) both sides have sufficient liquidity for simultaneous execution, (3) Market Scanner and arb-detector both independently confirm the opportunity.
rules.enforcement: Orchestrator consensus logic — hardcoded, not configurable. Arbitrage carve-out enforced via separate code path with independent validation (see arb-detector skill).

rules.name: Dissent Acknowledgment
rules.rule: When a trade executes on a split vote (3:2 or 4:1), the dissent report MUST be logged and the position size MUST be reduced by at least 25% from Kelly-optimal. Unanimous (5:0) trades get full Kelly-fraction sizing.
rules.enforcement: Orchestrator applies automatic size reduction on split consensus

rules.name: Maximum Concurrent Positions
rules.rule: No more than 10 concurrent open positions at any time. Portfolio concentration beyond this level creates correlated risk that consensus cannot mitigate.
rules.enforcement: Portfolio Tracker blocks new ExecutionOrders when limit reached

rules.name: Time-to-Resolution Minimum
rules.rule: Do not enter markets resolving in less than 2 hours unless executing a paired-contract arbitrage (which is time-insensitive). Short-resolution markets have high volatility and limited time for edge to materialize.
rules.enforcement: Market Scanner filters on resolution deadline

rules.name: Kelly Fraction Cap
rules.rule: Use half-Kelly (0.5x Kelly-optimal) as the default position sizing. Full Kelly is too aggressive for prediction markets given model uncertainty. Quarter-Kelly (0.25x) for markets with high agent disagreement.
rules.enforcement: Kelly Sizer skill applies fraction based on consensus strength

rules.name: No Override Without Human Approval
rules.rule: No agent, orchestrator component, or automated process may disable or modify these rules. Only a human operator with direct CLAUDE.md file access can change risk parameters. The system must treat CLAUDE.md as immutable at runtime.
rules.enforcement: CLAUDE.md must be set to read-only permissions at OS level (chmod 444 / attrib +R) during trading sessions. Portfolio Tracker must perform a SHA-256 hash check of CLAUDE.md at startup and compare against a committed known-good hash; halt trading if mismatch detected. Changes require git commit and manual restart.

subagent_orchestration.description: How Claude Code's native subagent system is used to run the 5 specialist agents in parallel.
subagent_orchestration.pattern: The Orchestrator is implemented as the primary Claude Code session. For each parliament vote, it spawns 5 subagents using Claude Code's built-in agent dispatch mechanism. Each subagent receives: (1) its specialist system prompt, (2) the CandidateMarket JSON, (3) its domain-specific data feeds, and (4) access only to MCP tools relevant to its domain (e.g., Crypto Agent gets on-chain tools but not news tools). Subagents run in parallel with a 30-second timeout. Results are collected as structured JSON.

agent_dispatch_config.retry_policy: No retries — timeout means the agent could not form a view in time, which is informative
agent_dispatch_config.isolation: Each subagent has its own system prompt, its own tool permissions, and its own data context. No shared state between agents during a voting session.

result_schema.sources: string[], at least 1 source required unless ABSTAIN
result_schema.domain_signals: object, agent-specific structured data supporting the vote
result_schema.processing_time_ms: integer, how long the agent took to analyze

progressive_signal_loading.description: Mechanism for incrementally adding or removing agents and data feeds without rebuilding the system. The Parliament is designed as a plug-in architecture where new specialist agents can be registered, existing agents can have their data feeds updated, and the consensus threshold adjusts automatically.
mechanism: Agent Registry: a JSON config file listing all active agents with their system prompts, tool permissions, and data feed configurations. Adding a new agent = adding an entry to this registry.
Dynamic Consensus Threshold: threshold is defined as ceil(n_agents * 0.6), so 3/5, 4/6, 4/7, etc. This maintains the ~60% supermajority requirement as agents are added.
Data Feed Routing: each agent's data feeds are defined in its registry entry. The Orchestrator's data loading step reads these configs and prepares isolated data packages dynamically.
Hot-swap Capability: agents can be disabled (set active: false) without removing them, allowing A/B testing of parliament configurations.

Signal Priority Levels: data feeds can be tagged as 'critical' (must load before vote), 'supplementary' (load if available, proceed without), or 'background' (async, may arrive after vote starts). This prevents slow data feeds from blocking the entire parliament.
progressive_signal_loading.TODO_schemas: Define a CandidateMarketPackage schema specifying the exact structure of the pre-loaded data package each agent receives (base market JSON + domain-specific feed payloads + feed freshness timestamps). Also define an agent_registry_schema for the Agent Registry config file, specifying required fields (agent_id, system_prompt, tool_permissions[], data_feed_configs[], active: boolean) so the Orchestrator can validate registry entries and route domain-specific data correctly.

risks.description: All 5 agents use the same underlying LLM (Claude), creating correlated failure modes. If the base model has a systematic bias or blind spot, all agents may share it despite having different prompts and data.
risks.mitigation: Consider mixing model providers (e.g., 2 Claude agents, 1 GPT, 1 Gemini, 1 open-source) for true cognitive diversity. The swarm approach from MoonDev's framework queries multiple model providers in parallel for exactly this reason. Monitor for correlated errors across agents.

risks.description: Domain-specific data feeds may be stale, incomplete, or unavailable. If the geopolitics agent receives no diplomatic briefings, its vote quality degrades but it may still vote with false confidence.
risks.mitigation: Each agent must report data freshness in its vote response. If primary data feeds are unavailable, agent should ABSTAIN rather than guess. Implement data feed health monitoring with Telegram alerts on feed failures.

risks.description: Market conditions can change between parliament vote completion and order execution. A 60-second deliberation window may be too slow for fast-moving markets.
risks.mitigation: Slippage protection: Execution Engine rejects trades where price has moved >2% from analysis time. For arbitrage opportunities (paired contracts), bypass parliament for speed per the RISK-005 arbitrage carve-out — these are mathematically defined edges that require independent verification by both Market Scanner and arb-detector, not consensus. Time-sensitive markets get priority dispatch with shorter agent timeouts.

risks.description: The 23% ROI improvement was measured over only 14 days and 47 markets. This sample size is insufficient for statistical significance. The system may be overfitting to a specific market regime.
risks.mitigation: Run extended paper trading (minimum 30 days, 200+ markets) before deploying real capital. Track performance across multiple market categories and regimes. Implement walk-forward validation: train weights on historical data, validate on subsequent unseen period.

risks.description: If agents learn to agree with each other (prompt drift, shared training data updates), the consensus mechanism loses its value. The parliament degenerates into a single-agent system with extra steps.
risks.mitigation: Monitor inter-agent agreement rate. If it exceeds 85% over a 7-day window, it indicates loss of diversity. Trigger system prompt review and data feed isolation audit. Consider introducing a mandatory 'devil's advocate' rotation.

risks.description: Dependency on multiple external APIs (Polymarket, Kalshi, news feeds, on-chain analytics). Any API outage, rate limit, or breaking change can disable part or all of the system.
risks.mitigation: Implement graceful degradation: if non-critical MCP servers are down, remaining agents still vote with available data. If Execution Engine APIs are down, queue approved trades for execution when connectivity restores. Maintain API key rotation and backup endpoints.

risks.description: Automated trading on prediction markets may face regulatory scrutiny depending on jurisdiction. Kalshi is a CFTC-regulated Designated Contract Market (DCM); Polymarket operates offshore. Automated bot trading on regulated exchanges carries material legal risk.
risks.mitigation: Legal review required before deployment — obtain written opinion on operator jurisdiction, platform-specific compliance requirements, and automated trading permissibility. Maintain explicit operator jurisdiction documentation. Implement platform-specific kill switches that can disable trading on any single platform independently. Operate within platform ToS. Maintain full audit trail for regulatory compliance. Implement geographic restrictions if required. Monitor regulatory developments via the Geopolitics Agent's data feeds.

success_criteria.target: 20%+ improvement over single-agent approach on identical market set
success_criteria.measurement: A/B test: run parliament and single-agent on same markets for 30 days, compare total ROI

success_criteria.target: 74%+ on executed trades (vs ~60% single-agent baseline). A 'win' is defined as a resolved position where total return (payout minus cost minus all fees) is strictly positive. Positions exited early at a loss count as losses. Positions exited early at a profit count as wins. Unresolved positions are excluded from win rate calculation until resolved or exited.
success_criteria.measurement: Count of profitable resolved/exited trades / total resolved/exited trades executed by parliament

success_criteria.target: 50%+ reduction in average loss size compared to single-agent
success_criteria.measurement: Mean loss on losing trades: parliament vs single-agent baseline

success_criteria.target: Minority dissent accuracy > 60% when dissent quality score exceeds 70
success_criteria.measurement: Track outcomes of trades where high-quality dissent was overridden vs heeded

success_criteria.target: < 15% of peak bankroll at any point
System should refuse 40-60% of candidate markets (consensus not reached)
success_criteria.measurement: Count of NO_TRADE decisions / total markets evaluated by parliament

success_criteria.target: Full parliament vote cycle p50 < 60 seconds, p95 < 120 seconds from market dispatch to decision. Pre-fetched data packages must be delivered to agents at dispatch time to avoid live fetch delays consuming the 30-second agent timeout.
success_criteria.measurement: Timestamp logging on Orchestrator: dispatch_time to decision_time, plus per-agent processing_time_ms breakdown
success_criteria.timeframe: Per-session, with p50, p95 and p99 tracking

success_criteria.target: Inter-agent unanimous agreement rate < 40% (agents should disagree frequently to demonstrate genuine analytical diversity). Track full vote split distribution: 5:0, 4:1, 3:2, and no-consensus outcomes. Healthy distribution target: 5:0 < 20%, 4:1 ~ 30-40%, 3:2 ~ 25-35%, no-consensus ~ 15-25%.
success_criteria.measurement: Percentage of parliament sessions by vote split pattern (5:0, 4:1, 3:2, no-consensus). Alert if 5:0 rate exceeds 40% over rolling window (indicates diversity collapse).

notes:
Key insight from source material: the Parliament's edge comes NOT from any individual agent being smarter, but from the built-in mechanism of doubt that a single model cannot replicate. The most profitable wallets on Polymarket 'almost never bet on the same thing at the same time' — they think differently, and that diversity is exactly what makes each profitable. The architecture replicates this cognitive diversity synthetically through isolated contexts and specialized data feeds.

The Science Agent anomaly is particularly important: it dissented more often than any other agent (19/47 markets), and when it was the sole dissenter against 4 agreeing agents, it was correct 4 out of 5 times (n=5 pilot sample, 80% accuracy). CAVEAT: This 5-sample result is directionally interesting but not statistically reliable — it must be validated over 30+ solo-dissent events before being treated as a durable edge. Those 4 correct dissents prevented $890 in avoided losses in the pilot. If the pattern holds at scale, the Dissent Analyzer is arguably the most important component in the entire architecture, not the consensus mechanism.

The harness architecture (from claw-code) provides the runtime context scoping pattern: agents 'know their role' before the conversation starts via injected system context, not through prompting. This is the foundation for agent specialization — each agent's worldview is shaped by its system prompt and its data feeds, not by user instructions.

Progressive signal loading allows the system to evolve: start with 5 agents, add a 6th (e.g., a 'Regulatory' agent) when that expertise gap is identified, and the consensus threshold adjusts automatically. The architecture is explicitly designed to grow.

Critical anti-pattern to avoid: giving all agents the same information. If every agent sees everything, they converge on the same conclusion, and the parliament becomes a single agent with 5x the cost and zero additional insight. Information isolation between agents is not a nice-to-have — it is the fundamental mechanism that creates the edge.
